newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile politicians slam officer's release from jail.
newsitem.headline: Chile politicians slam officer's release from jail.

text.p: Left-wing politicians criticised on Wednesday the freeing of an army officer who was jailed for setting fire to two young Chileans during a 1986 demonstration, killing one and maming the other.

Retired lieutenant Pedro Fernandez was released on Tuesday after serving a 600-day sentence for the murder of Rodrigo Rojas, a young photographer who resided in Washington, and the severe burns suffered by student Carmen Gloria Quintana.
"(The release) is the result of a benevolent judgment that did not match the gravity of the crime," said Socialist Party president Camilo Escalona. "At the time we said the ruling was a joke."

Fernandez was the first officer to be released from the top-security Punta Peuco jail, which has been built to house members of the armed forces imprisoned for human rights abuses during General Augusto Pinochet's military regime.
Rojas was the son of a Chilean exile living in Washington and was visiting Chile during a protest against Pinochet.

He and Quintana were detained on July 2, 1986, by an army patrol commanded by Fernandez, who doused the two youths with gasoline and set fire to them. They were severely burned and then left on a roadside near Santiago's airport.
Rojas died of his burns four days later, while Quintana received plastic surgery in Chile and abroad for her injuries.
